allOf.$comment: The operation branch: a plan that verifies rather than measures (plan.md 11-21). It holds for an `operation` block, and, since 2026-09-25, for a plan carrying `trap_steps` and no `goal_id`: placing a trap and having the person confirm a bead is held verifies a setup and measures nothing, so it takes no goal, no observable and no S3 to S5, exactly as a piezo verification step does. Proposed by microscope-20260924-6 when the first trap plan of the double-well day could not otherwise be written without claiming a record length it does not record. A plan with trap_steps AND a goal is a measurement plan and takes the full pipeline. Since 2026-10-03 the same holds for `focus_search` (plan.md 11-24): a search with no goal finds a plane and measures nothing about the sample, and a search with a goal takes the full pipeline.

definition.description: Kept for now and no longer required: the definition lives in contracts/observables.json, and a card that restates it holds a second copy that drifts -- eight cards had already drifted from the vocabulary by 2026-09-18. Name the observable and the definition, the estimator and the window come with it by reference. This property is due to be removed once every card has dropped it; 5.4 still asks for the definition and that sentence is the architecture seat's to settle before then.

system_configuration.description: What it is measured with, not only how (4.5.3, 4.6.7)

selectors.description:
The discrete settings this plan commands. Part of WHAT IT IS MEASURED WITH rather than a condition, because a condition points into numbers[] by name and a selector is not a number.

Added 2026-09-21, when S5 could not write an acquire action: widefield_inline declares two detectors, both Kinetix 22, and the device table says the arms differ only by the dichroic in the port -- so which camera collects is the csuw1_port setting, and this object had additionalProperties false and nowhere to put it. The plan knew the answer and the contract could not hold it.

preconditions.description:
What an axis required OF THE PLAN rather than of a value. common.schema.json's `precondition` says it plainly -- **it does not intersect, it propagates**: if any axis returns one the plan must carry it, and folding it into an allowed_set would see it silently dropped the first time S4 took an intersection.

This slot did not exist until 2026-09-21 and the omission had already cost something: `conditions` requires every entry to point at a `numbers[]` name, a precondition names no number, so **S5 was discarding A4's `verified_selectors` without saying it did**. A rule a schema states and no field can hold is a rule that runs on whoever remembers it.

NOT `required`, because a plan with no preconditions is ordinary. What is not ordinary is a plan missing one an axis returned -- and no schema can see that, because the axis cards are other files. That comparison is a check and it is owed.

parameter.description: the name the axis used, so the two match without reading prose

requires.description: what the plan must do, carried from the axis as an instruction and not paraphrased. Restating it in the planner's own words would put one rule in two wordings, and by the next revision it would be two rules (P3)

from_axis.description: which axis required it. A precondition that cannot name its axis is one the plan invented, and a plan does not get to require things of itself

basis.description: what the axis stood on, carried across unchanged

conditions.description: Every condition points at numbers[] by name; it never restates a value (5.2)

actions.description: What will be done to the instrument. reversible: false forces individual approval when it rests on E4/E5 (2.1 rule 3, check 22).

line.description: Which light line of the device this action drives, named exactly as the device reports it (GREEN, NIR, ...). Every parameter of the action applies to that line; two lines take two actions. Absent when the device has no lines. The runtime picks the binding whose line equals this one and refuses when a quantity has bound lines and the action names none or one no binding carries (microscope card 098 part 5; mm_bindings line, librarian card 062 as amended 2026-10-27).

stop_criteria.description: Declared before execution. Chosen afterwards they are narration, not results (5.4). Each one should say what being met means (on_met), so result.outcome is read rather than inferred -- an operator today tells a planned ending from a fault by whether the criterion fired earlier than the last planned chunk, and a distinction drawn by inference is one the schema should draw. It is not required yet, and the reason is not oversight: the plan cards that would have to gain it are pinned by a signed plan_approval, and adding a field changes the hash and voids it (5.5). Requiring it takes a corrected revision, which only a person can approve. Until then an agent's own standing orders can require what this schema cannot.

compare_arms.description: required when purpose is compare: arms may differ only in the compared variable (check 34)

targets.description: The accuracy the plan was built to meet, pinned at the moment it was built. A plan_approval fixes the plan and not the goal, so a plan that pointed at the goal's target would have its accuracy move after approval with nothing recording that it had (5.3.1).

sweep.description: A characterize over a product space. A card carries `sweep` OR `compare_arms` and NEVER BOTH -- a card carrying both is asking two questions. The two are not separated by how many variables move but by what the card claims at the end: compare_arms claims something about THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO STATES, which is why check 34 requires one variable to move so the difference can be attributed; a sweep claims something about A FUNCTION OVER A DOMAIN, where no point is privileged and there is nothing to attribute to one change. A one-arm compare is meaningless and a one-point sweep is just a run.

axes.description: The quantities that move and the levels they take, so `is this grid complete` is an answerable question. Without it a deliberately empty cell -- a corner skipped because it diverges -- cannot be recorded at all.

levels.description: names in numbers[]; a level never restates a value (5.2)

points.description: The condition sets actually performed. INVARIANT: every point shares every condition except the ones the axes name. Both fields are required together because neither says it alone -- axes without points cannot record which cells were skipped, and points without axes cannot say whether a missing corner was dropped or never in the grid. Together a gap is VISIBLE rather than silent, the same reason a stop criterion is declared before a run rather than after. THE INVARIANT IS NOT LITERAL AND NOT OPEN, settled 2026-09-23 when an execution seat asked which. Read literally -- only an axis parameter may differ -- a per-point timestep cannot be a condition at all and the operator has to derive it at S6, which moves an S4 decision into a stage that is meant to be deterministic and to decide nothing; it also leaves `varies_with` producing nothing, since an axis card could declare a bound varies with an axis and the plan would have nowhere to put the varied value. Read open -- any condition may differ -- the invariant constrains nothing and a point could differ in an unrelated parameter with no one seeing. SO: a condition may differ between points exactly when SOME AXIS CARD'S INTERVAL FOR THAT PARAMETER CARRIES `varies_with`. That is one step removed from the axes and no further, it is machine-readable on both sides, and it keeps the gap visible, which is what the invariant is for.

skipped.description: present when this cell of the grid was deliberately not run; says why

smoke.description: How much smaller the smoke run is, declared before anything runs so the operator never chooses it (task 023). `record_fraction` names a number in numbers[] (unit 1, 0 < value <= 1) that shortens the record at the same save interval, so particle steps and saved frames shrink together and the two cost terms keep their ratio. A smoke run is calibration; its output never becomes a result card for the question.

operation.description: An OPERATION PLAN: a move that verifies rather than measures (plan.md 11-21, settled 2026-09-24). No S3 to S5: a verification move measures nothing about the sample, so the seven axes have nothing to decide. Six conditions, of which the schema holds the shape and check 86 the rest: one device, and one axis per move; every commanded position inside the envelope's limits, checked by code before anything is sent, a missing limit refusing; each move's size and count written here and approved by the person through the ordinary plan_approval, with the bench; position read back before and after each move; what it verifies and what would falsify it, stated; reversible only. What it finds -- a channel mapping, a direction, a tracking error -- is a fact about the instrument and leaves as a result card naming the observation. It does not cover a measurement bound for the store, first focus-finding, or anything irreversible.

device.description: the one device every move commands

verifies.description: what the operation establishes, in words

falsified_by.description: the observation that would show the thing verified is not so

target_um.description: the absolute position commanded, in um. Absolute, not relative: a relative step re-sent after a lost reply moves twice, and an absolute target can be checked against the envelope before anything is sent

role.description: what the step is for. `direction_finding` is the only role Z may have, besides `return`, until the piezo-Z direction is recorded. `approach` brings an axis to where a sine starts: the controller rests at its floor, so a sine centred mid-range begins with a long move, and the plan carries that move explicitly rather than letting the first sine point make it

ramp_um_per_s.description: optional: move at this rate rather than in one jump, written as position writes paced from the integer index. The prior project ramped its long moves; whether one is needed is the person's, approved with the plan

axis.description: X and Y only. Z never takes periodic motion under an operation plan

points_per_period.description: the sine is written as this many absolute position writes per period, from the integer index, never an accumulated phase

host_timed.description: always true: the controller's own waveform generator is refused while the unit it reads is unmeasured here (the 314 um incident)

start.description: where the sine's first point is. `minimum` is centre minus amplitude (a cosine phase), and so on. The approach step before it must land exactly there. microscope-20260924-2's first sine design started at its minimum, so that the approach from the controller's rest position was 10 um rather than 300

focus_search.description: A FOCUS SEARCH on the Z drive (plan.md 11-24 and 13.2, added 2026-10-03 by manager-microscope-20261003-1). Two forms, as trap_steps: with a goal_id it sits beside the full pipeline and lifts none of it; with NO goal_id it is operation-style, purpose verify, no goal or observable. THE BRANCH IS A JUDGEMENT AND THE COMMAND IS NOT: whoever decides -- the metric maximum or a model -- picks one of `branches`, and the dispatcher derives the move from this block's fields alone. step_up is the last encoder read plus step_um and step_down the last read minus step_um, each sent as an ABSOLUTE target, because a relative move re-sent after a lost reply would move Z twice; in_focus, no_sample_here and unsure move nothing. Every command carries `from` naming the field it came from (check 14). THE Z FOUND IS AN ENCODER READ, never a decider's number. A target_z_um handed over from a coarse stage is a TARGET and not a destination: the search walks from retract toward it with the clearance comparison live at every step, and never jumps to it (card 026). PFS IS OFF for the whole search (4.6.8 interlock 3): a held focus fights a sweep. THE SEARCH CHANGES NO OUTPUT: illumination is what the plan set before it, and its frames are charged to A3's sample-health budget. THE Z DRIVE IS OPENED ONLY HERE, through the operator's exemption for an approved plan, and is never added to SOFTWARE_MAY_COMMAND. What the schema cannot compare, check 88 does at commit time: range_um inside the person's focus_z_<objective>_min/_max for this block's objective, a missing limit refusing; range_um a range; target_z_um inside range_um; step_um no larger than the range; and the named action on stand_ti2e and reversible. The run-time gate checks the same against the person's hand-over objective, which a commit cannot know. Success is declared before starting: the person's manual focus on the same fields is the reference, the metric maximum the baseline, the tolerance a fraction of the depth of field taken from the store, and hits, misses and unsure counted apart -- unsure is an abstention and is not a miss.

action.description: the id of the action in actions[] this search is dispatched as; it must command stand_ti2e and be reversible (check 88)

objective.description: the objective in place, spelled as the tweezers limits spell it (40x, 60x, 100x), so one objective has one token across the envelope. focus_z_<this>_{min,max} must exist in the microscope's envelope, and it must equal the person's hand-over statement, or the gate refuses. A DRY LENS THE PERSON HAS RELEASED STILL HAS BOTH KEYS: released means the person writes wide values for it, and never that the keys are absent. An absent key refuses for every objective, dry or immersion, and is never read as unlimited (the person's word of 2026-10-02, held to P0)

read_back.description: the Z found is the Z drive's encoder read after the decision, never a number the decider gave

pfs.description: PFS off before the first Z command and for the whole search (4.6.8 interlock 3)

approach_from.description: the search starts from the retracted Z and walks; it never jumps to a target

target_z_um.description: optional. An ABSOLUTE encoder Z handed over from a coarse stage, which the walk heads toward. A target, not a destination: reaching it is not finding focus

range_um.description: the ABSOLUTE encoder Z the search may visit, inside the person's focus_z_<objective> limits

step_um.description: the size of one step_up or step_down, in um of encoder Z

max_moves.description: the ceiling on moves; reaching it ends the search as not found, never as found

max_extensions.description: how many times the search may extend its range at the top end, a whole number of at least 0. A METHOD CHOICE: it carries no source and no grade, as max_moves does not. Required, with no default, because the copied search core takes it as a required argument (card 059); 0 means the search never extends

metric_arguments.description: the classical metrics' two size arguments (card 059). Both are METHOD CHOICES: the plan's own, with no source and no grade, as a target or a tolerance carries none. They are integers because the code takes them as integers

bin_px.description: the bin size, in px, for the peak-brightness metric

blocks_per_side.description: the block grid, in blocks per side, for the block scores

verdict_thresholds.description: the five thresholds the copied verdict (focus_verdict.from_sweep) takes as required arguments, with no defaults (card 063). METHOD CHOICES, like max_extensions, by architecture's ruling of 2026-10-07: no source and no grade. They decide only when the verdict abstains, and cannot move Z past anything, because the envelope and check 88 bound every step whatever they say. The person chose on 2026-10-02 to proceed with provisional values and settle them later against focus found by hand at the bench. All five are required: a missing one refuses here, and the decider refuses a plan without them

min_dynamic_range_adu.description: the least spread of pixel values, in ADU, for a frame to be read at all

min_contrast.description: the least contrast, as a fraction, for a sweep to show a focus

min_frames.description: the fewest frames a sweep needs before the verdict says anything but unsure

dropout_tolerance.description: how far a frame's mean may fall, as a fraction of the median frame mean, before it counts as a light dropout and not a focus change

max_saturated.description: the largest fraction of pixels at the camera ceiling a frame may carry and still be read

camera_ceiling.description: the camera's full-scale count in the readout mode the search uses, in ADU. A FACT ABOUT THE CAMERA, unlike the method choices beside it, so it is never written here as a value. It names EXACTLY ONE of two things. `number`: an entry in this card's numbers[] in ADU whose source is kb:, so the grade is derived from the store and never self-reported. `gap`: the gap_id of an entry in this card's kb_gaps, which is what a plan carries while the store has no such count -- true on 2026-10-05, when the store held the adapter's self-reported BitDepth 16 and a record of the camera misreporting its own bit depth, and no measured full-scale count. A GAP IS NEVER A DEFAULT: a plan naming one is valid and may be approved, and the code that reads it refuses to run the search rather than substitute a value. Check 88 checks that the name resolves

branches.description: the choices the decider may make, each a typed branch. in_focus and unsure are always among them: a search with no way to abstain forces a guess

decided_by.description: who picks the branch. Either way the command is derived from this block, and the metric maximum is the baseline in success

computed.description: computed by code from the frame, never by a model

illumination.description: the search touches no output; its frames are charged to A3's sample-health budget

fields.description: how many fields are searched and compared

depth_of_field.description: the depth of field the tolerance is a fraction of. A FACT ABOUT THE OPTICS, so it names EXACTLY ONE of two things, as camera_ceiling does: `number`, an entry in this card's numbers[] in a length unit, either MEASURED (source kb: and an entry the store has) or COMPUTED (source computed:, with inputs naming the store's derived_quantity entry of symbol depth_of_field, since the formula's inputs -- emission wavelength, immersion index -- are the sample's own and the value is the card's to compute, its grade derived as for any computed number); or `gap`, the gap_id of an entry in this card's kb_gaps. Until 2026-10-07 this was a bare kb: string, nothing checked that the entry existed, and every fixture cited an entry nobody had entered -- manager-librarian-20261007-1 found it. A gap is never a default: the plan is valid, and its success criterion cannot be judged until the store holds the value

trap_steps.description: TRAP STEPS for the optical tweezers, inside a measurement plan (added 2026-09-25, proposed by microscope-20260924-6 for the double-well run, card 049). The `operation` shape cannot hold them: it requires a position read back before and after each move, and the Tweez300 reports nothing back, so that could never be met, and its moves carry no trap or strength. TWO FORMS. With a goal_id it sits BESIDE the full pipeline's fields and lifts none of them: a measurement plan, with its goal, observable and S3 to S5. With NO goal_id it is an operation-style plan (5ab8116; plan.md 11-21 at 0f5914b): it verifies a setup and measures nothing, so it takes no goal or observable, purpose is verify, and its criteria point at its own targets. For a blind channel, two of the operation conditions are substituted, not dropped: one trap per step, with both coordinates checked; and a hold_for_person after every step a later step relies on, such as a caught bead, since a frame may record it but is not a read-back of the trap. Each step names an action of the same id, and the dispatcher derives exactly one TCP command per step. POSITIONS ARE ABSOLUTE ONLY: a relative move re-sent after a lost reply would move a trap twice, and the shape has no field for one. What the schema cannot check, the exemption checks before the first command is sent: every x and y inside tweezers_trap_position_<objective>_{min,max} for this block's objective, which must equal the hand-over's; every strength inside tweezers_trap_strength_{min,max}; each position step's distance from that trap's previous absolute position at most tweezers_trap_step_max, a first position with no known start refusing; and any missing limit refusing. A hold_for_person step stops the dispatcher until the person answers in the seat's window, because the tweezers are blind and a caught bead can only be the person's statement or a frame. The beam is assumed on after any step.

objective.description: the objective in place; tweezers_trap_position_<this>_{min,max} must exist for it, and it must equal the person's hand-over statement, or the exemption refuses

read_back.description: always none: the Tweez300 has no query of any kind, and a return code is not a read-back

trap.description: the plan's own name for the trap, e.g. trap_1 (the deeper, stiffer one by the shared naming) or trap_2

x_um.description: ABSOLUTE position in um in the Tweez300's calibrated field, relative to the image centre

y_um.description: ABSOLUTE position in um in the Tweez300's calibrated field, relative to the image centre

strength.description: relative strength, 0 to 1, the Tweez300's own format. It shares out the laser power; the total is the person's hand

trap.description: the plan's own name for the trap, e.g. trap_1 (the deeper, stiffer one by the shared naming) or trap_2

strength.description: relative strength, 0 to 1, the Tweez300's own format. It shares out the laser power; the total is the person's hand

trap.description: the plan's own name for the trap, e.g. trap_1 (the deeper, stiffer one by the shared naming) or trap_2

x_um.description: ABSOLUTE position in um in the Tweez300's calibrated field, relative to the image centre

y_um.description: ABSOLUTE position in um in the Tweez300's calibrated field, relative to the image centre

trap.description: the plan's own name for the trap, e.g. trap_1 (the deeper, stiffer one by the shared naming) or trap_2

statement.description: what the person is asked to confirm before the dispatcher goes on, e.g. that a bead is caught in trap_1

watcher.description: The RUN-TIME WATCHER, in shadow mode (plan.md 13.4, settled by the person on 2026-10-17; added by manager-microscope-20261003-1). A plan that wants its run watched declares this block, and the person's approval covers it. THE WATCHER RECORDS AND NEVER ACTS: no field here names an action, a threshold or a stop, and no code path runs from an answer to the stop channel or to a prompt for the person until plan.md 13.4 records the person's decision on a threshold. Every number here is a METHOD CHOICE, the plan's own, with no source and no grade, as focus_search's max_moves and metric_arguments carry none; the one fact about the world, the camera ceiling, is named exactly as focus_search names it. NO FIELD HAS A DEFAULT, in this schema or in code: a run whose plan lacks one does not guess it. WHICH BACKEND ANSWERS IS NOT HERE. It is a run argument (--backend), because in shadow mode it changes nothing the approval covers, and the record says which one answered.

options.description: The answers a backend may give, IN ORDER; the order is recorded with every question. as_planned and unsure are in every list. Every other option names, in `about`, the rendered value it is about, so a flag has a deterministic route to a claim in deviations.json. The first list is plan.md 13.1's: as_planned, particles_lost, drifting, focus_lost, unsure. NO CODE HOLDS A DEFAULT LIST, and a model adds no option: the list grows by plan. Ids are unique.

about.description: the name of the rendered value this option is about, e.g. particle_count, drift_px, focus_score

cadence_s.description: seconds between two watcher ticks: one hardware snapshot, one rendered state, at most one question. The person approves it with the plan; plan.md names no number and the code holds no default

question_budget_s.description: the longest a question may wait for an answer. Past it the question is recorded as watcher_unanswered, why time_budget, and the run never waits on it

image.description: the image side of the state, with every argument the renderer needs and none it may assume

frame_stats.description: the arguments of the copied focus_classical.frame_stats; every statistic it returns is rendered

camera_ceiling.description: the camera's full-scale count for the readout mode the run uses, in ADU, which frame_stats needs for the saturated fraction. Named exactly as focus_search names it: `number`, an entry in this card's numbers[] whose source is kb:, or `gap`, the gap_id of an entry in kb_gaps. A gap is never a default: with a gap the saturated fraction is rendered absent, never computed against an assumed count

intensity.description: WHOLE-FRAME intensity, normalised to the SETTLED level: never read through a mask fixed at frame 0, and never normalised to frame 0 (the 2026-09-24 photostability lesson in microscope_agent/CLAUDE.md: a source sits about 3.5% low for its first seconds)

settle_after_s.description: seconds after the run's last light-source command whose read-back matched; the whole-frame total from then on is the level, and before it normalised intensity is rendered absent, labelled settling

drift.description: drift as a whole-frame shift against a reference frame

reference_frame.description: the frame index the shift is measured against

particles.description: the particle count, from a deterministic detector whose every argument is here

frames.description: WHETHER THE BACKEND IS GIVEN IMAGES, and how they are made (plan.md 13.4 items 4 and 5, the person's change of 2026-10-19 at 2fde65b1). A plan field, not a run argument, because what leaves the building is the approval's to cover. When `given` is true the backend receives two images beside the text: the current frame and the run's reference frame, the first frame after the light settles (intensity.settle_after_s). Both are made by one versioned conversion to an ordinary 8-bit image with these parameters: a downscale, a contrast stretch whose limits are recorded per frame, and saturated pixels marked against the camera ceiling. THE RAW 16-BIT FRAME NEVER LEAVES THE RENDERER. A local and a hosted model get the same images. `given` has no default: a watcher block says true or false. With the camera ceiling a gap, saturated pixels cannot be marked, and the conversion refuses rather than marking against an assumed count

stretch.description: the contrast stretch; the limits it computes are recorded for each frame in watcher_state

saturated.description: how a pixel at or above the camera ceiling is marked in the 8-bit image

judgements.description: plan.md 13.5's judgements DM-1, DM-2 and DM-4, which a plan that wants them declares here; DM-3 is the `watcher` block. EVERY ONE RECORDS ONLY: no field here is a threshold or an action, and none may be added until the person chooses a judgement's threshold from the record, in plan.md. The backend is a run argument, as the watcher's is. Whether images are given is each judgement's own `frames`, the watcher's shape, because what leaves the building is the approval's to cover. A METHOD CHOICE throughout: no source, no grade, no default.

dm1.description: DM-1, are the particles the fixed code detected suitable for the planned measurement. Asked after detection, before a field is measured; nothing is moved or skipped on it

items.description: run_start; before_measure:<id> or after_measure:<id>, where <id> is one of this plan's stop_criteria ids. These are the moments the orchestrator reaches and names (card 081, 99c02ddb). Any other name would be a point the run never reaches, so the judgement would never be asked and only run_ended's unreached list would show it; the schema refuses it instead. `stop` is DM-4's alone

points.description: every moment the run reaches at which this judgement is asked; while it records only, it is asked at each of them, normal ones included

reason_codes.description: the reason codes an answer may give, declared by the plan; a model adds none

dm2.description: DM-2, is this field of view suitable. Asked before a measurement starts; it leads to no move, and cannot until the XY design exists and is bench-checked

items.description: run_start; before_measure:<id> or after_measure:<id>, where <id> is one of this plan's stop_criteria ids. These are the moments the orchestrator reaches and names (card 081, 99c02ddb). Any other name would be a point the run never reaches, so the judgement would never be asked and only run_ended's unreached list would show it; the schema refuses it instead. `stop` is DM-4's alone

points.description: every moment the run reaches at which this judgement is asked; while it records only, it is asked at each of them, normal ones included

reason_codes.description: the reason codes an answer may give, declared by the plan; a model adds none

dm4.description: DM-4, can the failure's cause be identified, and as what. Asked after a stop, on the saved evidence including the rolling pre-stop buffer of reduced frames (Q5); it starts no recovery

items.description: DM-4 is asked after a stop, on the saved evidence, and the orchestrator reaches that moment only as `stop`

points.description: every moment the run reaches at which this judgement is asked; while it records only, it is asked at each of them, normal ones included

cause_labels.description: the plan's cause labels, in order. The first list is 13.5's: focus_drift, particle_lost, aggregation_or_interaction, stage_or_sample_drift, illumination_or_signal_issue, camera_or_acquisition_issue, unknown. unknown is always present and is a NO

pre_stop_buffer.description: The rolling pre-stop buffer (plan.md 4.6.1 at 578a20ee, the person's Q5 at 04e3985f): a stop keeps the last `length_s` seconds before it and saves them, with lamps off and shutters closed first as the abort order says, and nothing emits light after a stop. A top-level block because it binds for every plan whose run can stop; the judgements block reads it and does not own it. NO DEFAULT: a plan that can reach a device and has no block is refused by the operator (2.1 rule 2: unstated is a stop), naming 4.6.1; a simulation or replay plan that reaches no device is exempt. The schema cannot tell those apart or an old record from a new plan, so the refusal lives in the operator, where a plan reaches a device, and the plans committed before this block keep their hashes and approvals and refuse to run until revised. Zero is allowed only if written: the person may choose to keep nothing, and the plan then says so. THERE IS NO RATE FIELD: the buffer holds only copies of frames the run already acquires, taken from the frame tap's tee, never triggers an acquisition or light, and records its own rate. Its raw frames stay whole in the run folder; a model is given only reduced copies (13.4 item 4). A METHOD CHOICE: no source, no grade.

length_s.description: seconds of frames kept before a stop; 0 written means the person chose to keep none
